references.text: Isaiah prophesies that the Lord will visit with thunder, earthquake and great noise – a parallel to the cosmic signs and earthquakes Jesus describes. [ref:Jes 29:6|Isaiah 29:6]

Joel prophesies about signs in heaven and on earth – blood, fire and pillars of smoke, the sun is darkened and the moon becomes like blood – before the great day of the Lord comes. [ref:Joel 2:30-31|Joel 2:30-31]
Matthew's parallel passage: Jesus says that people will rise up against people and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places. [ref:Matt 24:7|Matthew 24:7]
Mark's parallel passage about end-time signs: people against people, kingdom against kingdom, earthquakes in many places and famines. [ref:Mark 13:8|Mark 13:8]
In Revelation a great earthquake is described as one of the signs at the opening of the sixth seal, parallel to the great earthquakes Jesus predicts. [ref:Rev 6:12|Revelation 6:12]
In Revelation a great earthquake occurs where a tenth of the city falls and seven thousand people are killed – terrifying signs from heaven. [ref:Rev 11:13|Revelation 11:13]

Great signs in heaven are described in Revelation – a woman clothed with the sun and a great fiery red dragon – parallel to the great signs from heaven Jesus mentions. [ref:Rev 12:1-3|Revelation 12:1-3]
Peter quotes Joel's prophecy about signs in heaven and on earth, which links the events of Pentecost to Jesus' predictions about cosmic signs. [ref:Acts 2:19-20|Acts 2:19-20]
Later in the same speech Jesus expands on the signs: signs in sun, moon and stars, and people will faint from fear because of what is coming upon the earth. [ref:Luke 21:25-26|Luke 21:25-26]
God says that he can send pestilence (plague) and famine as discipline over his people – a background for the plagues Jesus predicts. [ref:2 Chron 7:13-14|2 Chronicles 7:13-14]
